title: DECISION: Provider ctx zeroization is contract-enforced, not framework-backstopped
description:
The framework calls sess_free(ctx)/key_free(ctx) and trusts the provider to memzero_explicit before kfree. Framework-owned buffers (inbuf, outbuf, fd_state) are zeroized independently. Provider ctx is not — the framework holds a void* of unknown size and cannot do so without memory pressure overhead (tracking ctx_size, keeping allocation alive across cleanup).

The contract in crypto2dev_provider.h lines 133-135 and 450-453 explicitly requires memzero_explicit over all sensitive fields before kfree. Enforcement is contract + code review + audit checklist item.

A reviewer or auditor who suggests adding ctx_size + framework-level zeroization: the answer is no — the memory pressure is not justified given the explicit contract and review gate. The risk (future provider omitting memzero_explicit) is accepted and mitigated by documentation and audit, not by runtime mechanism.
